production_only_result.note: The critical Vitest/tinypool/@vitest/mocker findings are development-test-toolchain findings. The frontend Docker runner installs with `npm ci --omit=dev`, so they are not in the runtime image; the deps and builder stages do install dev tools.

packages.name: next
packages.smallest_safe_remediation: After approval, run the official Next.js 15->16 upgrade/codemod and `npm install next@16.4.6`; rebuild, typecheck, lint, and rerun Playwright/axe. Do not hand-edit the nested postcss version.
packages.risk: Major framework upgrade; requires Node >=20.9.0 and review of Next.js 16 breaking changes. No upgrade was applied.

packages.name: postcss
packages.dependency_chain: next@15.5.29 -> node_modules/next/node_modules/postcss@8.4.31 (nested; root postcss@8.5.33 from Tailwind/Vite is a separate, non-vulnerable instance)
advisory_titles: PostCSS has XSS via Unescaped </style> in its CSS Stringify Output
PostCSS: Arbitrary file read and information disclosure via attacker-controlled sourceMappingURL in CSS comments
PostCSS: incomplete fix of GHSA-6g55-p6wh-862q - attacker-controlled sourceMappingURL reads arbitrary .map files when `from` is unset
PostCSS: Path Traversal in Previous Source Map Auto-Loading (sourceMappingURL) leads to Arbitrary .map File Disclosure
packages.smallest_safe_remediation: Same as `next`: upgrade Next.js to 16.4.6 with the codemod. A direct override of nested postcss is not the recommended release fix.
packages.risk: Build-time CSS processing; exposure depends on attacker-controlled CSS/source maps. No change was applied.

packages.name: zod
packages.dependency_chain: frontend-next package.json -> zod@3.25.76 (used by auth/register/login/Google BFF route schemas)
advisory_titles: Zod can exhaust memory while validating oversized constrained collections
packages.smallest_safe_remediation: After approval, `npm install zod@4.6.7`, then run typecheck, lint, build, Vitest and Playwright/axe; review the Zod 4 migration notes for schema/error-API changes.
packages.risk: Major validation-library upgrade affecting request schemas; no patched v3 line was reported. No change was applied.

packages.name: vitest
packages.dependency_chain: frontend-next package.json (dev) -> vitest@3.2.4; transitive @vitest/mocker@3.2.4 and tinypool@1.1.1
advisory_titles: When Vitest UI server is listening, arbitrary file can be read and executed
Vitest: Path Traversal / Arbitrary File Read via @vitest/mocker Redirect Mock (shared with @vitest/mocker)
packages.smallest_safe_remediation: After approval, `npm install --save-dev vitest@4.1.12`; verify lockfile resolves @vitest/mocker@4.1.12 and removes/replaces vulnerable tinypool; rerun Vitest, typecheck, build and Playwright/axe.
packages.risk: Dev-toolchain major upgrade; Node ^20 || ^22 || >=24 required (local Node v22.23.2 satisfies this). Critical UI-server issue is not exposed in the current local test invocation, but the toolchain finding remains open. No change was applied.

packages.name: @vitest/mocker
advisory_titles: Vitest: Path Traversal / Arbitrary File Read via @vitest/mocker Redirect Mock
Vitest: Code injection via unauthenticated manual mock registration
packages.smallest_safe_remediation: Covered by the approved `vitest@4.1.12` dev-toolchain upgrade; do not add a direct dependency.

packages.name: tinypool
advisory_titles: Tinypool: Prototype Pollution gadget in worker options leads to Remote Code Execution
Tinypool: Prototype Pollution Gadget to RCE in run() options
packages.fix_available: npm reports fixAvailable: true (safe target is supplied through the vitest@4.1.12 toolchain upgrade)
packages.smallest_safe_remediation: Covered by the approved `vitest@4.1.12` upgrade; verify with `npm ls tinypool`. Do not add an ad-hoc direct pin.
packages.risk: Test-only in this workspace; not present in the production-only Docker runner. No change was applied.

disposition: Not auto-fixed. Remaining fixes require semver-major Next.js and Zod upgrades plus a Vitest 4 toolchain migration; formal approval is required in this release-controlled workspace. Re-run both audit commands and attach fresh JSON after any approved change.
